newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban cross key pass to foes' territory.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban cross key pass to foes' territory.

text.p: Forces of the Taleban Islamic militia pushed through the strategic Salang Pass in northern Afghanistan on Tuesday, advancing deeper into opposition territory, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said the Taleban's advance, which included tanks, was a major breakthrough and had put the militia firmly in control of the southern and the northern ends of the pass.

The Taleban advance was held up when retreating opposition forces blew up a bridge about five km (three miles) north of the pass, but some of their troops marched on foot to reach the village of Khinjan in Baghlan province.
AIP said white Taleban flags fluttered in Khinjan, about 15 km (nine miles) north of the pass.
The Taleban's control of the strategic pass comes after two days of resistance from forces loyal to the ousted government's military commander Ahmed Shah Masood.

It will cut off the last link between Masood, who controls pockets of northeastern Afghanistan, and the Hezb-i-Wahadat, a mainly Shi'ite faction still fighting to retain control of central Afghanistan's Bamiyan province.

The Taleban had reached the 11,000-foot (3,350 m) pass, north of the capital Kabul, on Sunday, seeking to cross into opposition territory after a peace deal with a local pro-Masood commander, Basir Salangi.
However, opposition shelling on Monday and a bridge blown up by the retreating forces of Masood held them up for two days.
The fall of Mazar-i-Sharif, the main point of supply for opposition forces as well as their political capital, dealt them a severe blow.
They now control less than 10 percent of the country and are confined to mountainous territory in northeastern and central Afghanistan.

The remaining opposition forces are being squeezed by Taleban forces moving south from Mazar-i-Sharif and north from Kabul. Masood is holding out in his native Panjsher valley close to the Salang Pass.
